title: Squares of a Sorted Array
description: Given an integer array `nums` sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.
input_format: First line contains integer `n`, followed by `n` sorted integers.

sample_tests.explanation: After squaring, the array becomes [16,1,0,9,100]. Sorted: [0,1,9,16,100].

hints: Notice that the largest squares are at either end of the array due to negative values.
Use two pointers at start and end.
Compare squares and place the larger one from back to front in the result array.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[1:1+n]]
    res = [0] * n
    l, r = 0, n - 1
    idx = n - 1
    while l <= r:
        sl = nums[l] * nums[l]
        sr = nums[r] * nums[r]
        if sl > sr: res[idx] = sl; l += 1
        else: res[idx] = sr; r -= 1
        idx -= 1
    print(' '.join(map(str, res)))
